decisionRule: Confirmation OA (the owner's three behaviour asks), registered before any OA game was played. November 24, 2026 (UTC).
Origin. On November 24 the owner chose, for three behaviour fixes they had asked for and that measured flat in development
on the profile-v28 research trees: splits, "AI seats + Premium, after a check"; the flyer-dive guard, "Check, then adopt";
the Troll gift, "Check, then adopt". Each is a behaviour fix the owner asked for, so its strength gate is non-inferiority,
as for the keep-attack fix (v21), the rejection fixes (v22) and carrier cohesion (v32).
- FD, a19-flyer-dive-guard-v1. Owner, arena game eca8580f: "force flying single unit griffin not always a good idea, and I
had good coverage". Development (prod28f, pools 402 + 402): pooled +0.00 (95% -2.10 to +2.07).
- SS, a19-split-screen-v1. Owner: "premium for some reason always decides to split ranges instead of melee for some
reason. For example wolf is much better to split to cover, as it is 1x2 unit. But it depends. Looks like ai is not
trained to split well". Development (prod28s, can-change tasks): pooled +0.89 (95% -6.20 to +7.54).
- TG, a19-troll-gift-split-v1. Owner, staging game 7c0a741a: "he could've gifted with 1 troll instead of full stack to
crusader, and full stack coulve go for attack". Development (prod28g, 588 can-change tasks): pooled +0.17 (95% -2.01 to
+2.32). Confirmation TG was prepared on prod28g and never registered or played; OA replaces it.
Rules (each behind a per-seat switch, on for the candidate seat only; production has every switch off):
- FD (common src/ai/flyer_dive_guard.ts and the search driver's challenger filter; A19_FLYER_DIVE_GUARD_<LEFT|RIGHT>=1): in
laps 1-2, while the native decision of a melee flyer (any level) is a wait, the search drops every challenger that is a
move or a move-and-strike ending 4 or more cells (Chebyshev, between footprints) from every living ally and farther from
them than the flyer stands now.
- SS (common src/ai/split_screen.ts and tactical_split_placement.ts {screen}; A19_SPLIT_SCREEN_<LEFT|RIGHT>=1; the server's
split plan reads it): no shooter "cover" split is reserved; 1x2/2x1 stacks may be split; every slot left after the
aura/support/shield splits becomes a one-model split of the best cheap body (lowest level, rectangle first, melee before
shooter, largest stack).
- TG (common src/ai/wild_regeneration_gift.ts, candidates.ts, versions/v0_4.ts; A19_TROLL_GIFT_SPLIT_<LEFT|RIGHT>=1; the
server's split plan reads it): (1) no Wild Regeneration cast is offered to a stack while a smaller living allied stack
of its creature still holds the ability; (2) when the army has a Troll stack of at least two, no one-Troll stack and an
ally of level 3 or lower, not a Troll, with more HP per creature, the split plan adds a one-Troll cover split in a free
slot or in place of its last bait/cover split.
Tree: server 2655971 (profile v34; main is e6c7c30, docs only since) and common dbb349ff (profile v34), plus the three
rules (overlay sha256 in the registration) and the replay game-id override (research only: ranked_adapter.ts e91e1733, so
a replayed owner game keeps its game-id-seeded stones). Tree manifest e45a6f027a12e9e6f54608bd1bc3dfee02a9a1e95336930d99b3df1cc4e294df
(sha256 over the sorted sha256sum list of src/**/*.ts and node_modules/@heroesofcrypto/common/src/**/*.ts), identical on
basenode and x3d. Parity: with every switch off the tree reproduced the v34 override tree on 4 of 4 owner tasks.
Runner: life-run20.ts (life-run19 plus read-only probes; parity 1 of 1 against life-run19), life-pool20.sh. Both seats
play the production bot seat with deep fit at 4,000 rollout turns; offline play has no clock. An arm sets its switch for
the entrant (the candidate's seat) only, through HOC_RESEARCH_ENTRANT_SEAT_ENV.
Bank (populations):
- own and mir (natural): fresh seeds22 families 1700-2208 (allocate_v39, namespace decoy-path-20261123-v1; never drafted or
played before), fight r0 on maps 1, 3 and 4; the entrant drafted as the default (league-drafts15 seat MG:mix:0.5:2, as
the WC/SD/DP/TG banks), opponent S:B23:fast:K14 (own, owner-shaped strikers) or MG:mix:0.5:2 (mir); 1,527 tasks each.
- owner: the owner's 10 recent test-server games (the owner's real setup replayed on its seat, the AI seat on the v34
production re-draft), 32 fresh seeds per game (namespace owner-asks-oa-20261124-v1), 320 tasks.
- tgown and tgmir (TG only): the prepared TG banks, seeds22 families 1100-1699 (drafted with the Troll forced at level 2,
never played), the tasks whose army has a Troll: 731 and 534.
Census (setup only, outcome-blind, before this registration; 0 quality errors): every task under production, SS and TG.
Populations and played tasks (oa_lists.py):
- FD: tasks whose entrant fields a melee flyer at the production opening, all played: own 1,250, mir 1,185, owner 320.
- SS: every own, mir and owner task (3,374); played where the SS opening differs: 578, 519, 192. The others open
identically, so their games are identical and add 0.
- TG: tasks whose entrant fields a Troll at the production opening (own 213, mir 240, owner 96, tgown 731, tgmir 534);
played where the TG opening differs or either opening has two or more Troll stacks: 138, 114, 96, 507, 290. The others
add 0 (one Troll stack and the same opening: the casting rule cannot act).
- Control: every task some rule plays (3,729). Games: 8,918, plus 80 parity replays.
Analysis (oa_analyze.py): per rule, the candidate arm against the control, paired by task; points per game for the entrant
(win 100, draw 50, loss 0). Primary: the mean over the rule's whole population. Interval: 95% percentile of 10,000
bootstrap replicates (seed 20261124); natural and Troll tasks resample their draft-root family (seeds22 family, shared by
every map and population) with replacement, owner tasks keep their 10 games and resample seeds within each game.
Gates, for each rule X in FD, SS, TG, all required:
X1 non-inferiority: the primary 95% lower bound is at least -2 points.
X2 no population estimate of X is below -2 points.
X3 games with a quality error in X's arm are not more than the control's on X's played tasks.
X4 behaviour:
FD4: the guard removes at least one challenger, and the entrant's real melee-flyer stacks (two or more creatures when
first seen, not summoned) gone by an AI turn of lap 1 or 2 are, in the FD arm, not more than in the control.
SS4: over SS's played tasks, the SS openings have fewer shooter split stacks and more 1x2/2x1 split stacks than the
control's (a split stack: every stack of a creature beyond its first).
TG4: of the entrant's Wild Regeneration casts in TG-arm games whose opening has two or more Troll stacks, at least 75%
come from a smaller stack (rank 1 or more among its creature's opening stacks).
X5 parity: the first 20 own tasks of the control's and of X's list, replayed on the second host, reproduce their digests,
and every played game opens as its census did.
Reported, not gated: per-population estimates and changed games won and lost; FD's vetoes and the level-4 stacks' death
laps; SS's split counts; TG's gift census by stack (split, largest, lone).
Decision. A rule whose five gates pass is adopted with its switch on unless "0", as the next free A19 profile, in the order
FD, SS, TG among those that pass, and deployed under the standing instruction: FD for AI seats; SS for AI seats and Premium
"Arrange army" and its client projection, as the owner asked; TG's casting rule for AI seats, its carrier split in the
same split plan (AI seats and Premium "Arrange army"). A gain is claimed only if the primary lower bound is above zero.
Not claimed: a win rate against people. Caveat (server-35's fight study of the owner's 10 recent games, November 24): with
identical armies and setups the owner's own fight is worth about 28 points per game more than the AI-played owner seat,
which punishes lone arrivals less; a non-inferiority result here is a floor on the guard's value against the owner, and a
null is not evidence that it is useless. The rules are measured separately against production; adopted together, their
interaction is not measured (SS and TG both change the split plan). A rule that fails a gate is not adopted; its failure
stays recorded and it is not re-run or relabelled; the owner is told.
